text: IMHPA: July rainfall across the Canal watershed running ~40% below seasonal norm; El Nino suppressing rainy-season onset
Photos circulating of exposed shoreline around Gatun Lake; residents say level visibly lower than typical for late July
Routine maintenance dredging scheduled on the Houston Ship Channel next week; no transit impact expected
ACP Advisory to Shipping: sustained precipitation deficit in watershed; Gatun and Alhajuela lake levels below 5-year average; conservation measures under review
STRI hydrologists: Gatun Lake near 79 ft, several feet below normal mid-rainy-season levels; driest year since at least 2015-16 El Nino
Lock staff at Gatun reportedly briefed on water-saving protocols; rumor of draft cuts circulating among agents in Colon
Multiple Neopanamax boxships transiting with AIS-reported drafts 1-2 ft under design load; consistent with voluntary light-loading
Reuters: Panama Canal faces driest spell since 1950; authority weighs deeper draft restrictions as Gatun Lake falls
Port of Singapore berth utilization steady; no unusual congestion reported across transshipment hubs
ACP advisory: maximum authorized draft for Neopanamax locks reduced to 43.5 ft effective immediately; Panamax locks capped at 39.5 ft
Bloomberg: Panama Canal draft cut forces carriers to shed several hundred TEU per Neopanamax voyage; surcharge risk rises
Maersk advisory: weight restrictions in effect for Panama transits; some cargo may need alternate routing or transshipment
Pacific-side anchorage filling up: ~45 vessels holding off Balboa; average wait for unbooked ships climbing past 5 days
MiAmbiente reiterates watershed emergency: Gatun-Alhajuela basin supplies both canal operations and drinking water for ~2.5M people
Crew on a bulker reports 7 days waiting at the Atlantic anchorage near Colon; no firm transit time assigned
Rotterdam handles normal summer volumes; barge draft limits on Rhine easing after weekend rain
ACP advisory: daily booking slots reduced to 32 per day effective Aug 8, down from a typical 36-38; further measures possible if rains fail
Xeneta note: special transit-auction pricing already elevated; slot competition intensifying among LPG and container operators
Kpler: ~60 vessels now staged at anchorages on both entrances; queue skewed toward non-booked bulk and tanker tonnage
Hapag-Lloyd: customers advised of canal weight limits; evaluating per-container surcharges on Asia-US East Coast services
Forwarders in Panama report booking backlogs building; demurrage exposure rising at both Balboa and Cristobal
Environmental groups warn watershed deforestation is amplifying runoff variability; long-term water yield for locks at risk
Reuters: Panama Canal backlog tops 100 vessels; waiting time for ships without reservations reaches 10 days and climbing
Drewry: Asia-US East Coast composite rates firming as Panama constraints begin absorbing effective capacity on all-water strings
Weekly Gulf grain inspection volumes near seasonal average; barge rates steady at New Orleans elevators
TankerTrackers: first VLGC and LNG tonnage observed diverting toward Suez routing rather than wait for Panama slots
Unverified chatter: a special auction slot reportedly cleared near $800k — brokers calling it the start of bidding season
ACP: draft and slot restrictions to remain in place at least through Sept 10; measures will be reassessed if watershed rains recover
CMA CGM announces Panama Canal surcharge effective Sept 1; cites draft restrictions and slot scarcity on East Coast loops
Los Angeles anchorage counts remain minimal; terminal gate fluidity unchanged
LNG and LPG carriers skipping the canal via Suez or Cape; auction for one priority slot reportedly tops $1M
AIS shows ~120 vessels holding at both entrances; drifting/loitering patterns consistent with waits of 1-2 weeks
La Prensa: ACP evalua recortes adicionales si los niveles de Gatun no se recuperan; el administrador califica la sequia de historica
Vessel holding patterns now visible hundreds of miles offshore: an LPG carrier loitering deep in the Gulf of Panama awaiting a slot
Reuters: Panama Canal ship backlog hits ~150 vessels; average wait for non-booked ships near 21 days — up sharply in two weeks
Xeneta: special transit auction cleared at ~$2.4M for a single slot — roughly 20x the typical fee; bidding spreading to boxships
Hapag-Lloyd confirms Panama Canal Transit surcharge of ~$500/container effective September; cites restricted draft and slot scarcity
Displacement effect visible at Cartagena: feeder and relay traffic building as some services drop direct canal calls
Reroute traffic patterns emerging in the southwest Caribbean: vessels staging near Barranquilla while awaiting transit instructions
Asia-US East Coast spot rates up sharply week-over-week; analysts attribute part of the move to capacity absorbed by canal queue
Bloomberg: ACP deputy administrator calls it the canal's worst drought in modern history; cuts could persist into 2024
Forwarder chatter: auction bids for September slots already clearing $2M; shippers scrambling for alternatives
ACP: 32 daily slots and 43.5-ft draft cap maintained; backlog-clearance prioritized by booking order, not auction, for regular traffic
Queue estimate ~160 vessels total; some bulkers approaching three weeks at anchor; spaced convoys now routine
Auction premiums for priority transits reported near $2.9M — a record for canal access fees on top of standard tolls
Reuters: major carriers roll out broad Panama surcharges; shippers told to expect delays on US East Coast routes into Q4
Shippers report feeders congesting Balboa transshipment; some boxes rolled two sailings as lines re-sequence around slot scarcity
Water-risk analysts: Gatun basin stress is structural — canal trade-off between navigation draft and municipal supply sharpened by El Nino
